decisions.reason: As a flagship electrometer close to the firm's core dosimetry and QA business, it is likely to meet or be allowed time to meet aspirations, especially in an expanding firm with organisational slack.

Because this oncology risk-management software builds on the established software and radiation-therapy base, management would more likely continue refining and supporting it than withdraw it after only a short market period.
A CT image quality phantom fits the firm's broader medical-imaging QA capabilities, so under bounded rationality it would likely be retained while performance information accumulates.

This mammography phantom is more distant from the firm's main radiation-therapy focus, so aspirations are less certain and withdrawal risk is higher, but current growth and slack still favor giving it more time.

As another distant mammography QA product, it faces a relatively higher chance of falling short of aspirations, yet the firm's broad portfolio and expansion make continued trial more likely than immediate exit.
This imaging QA instrument line is both close to the established offer and presented as a strategic focus, which makes continued commitment and problem-solving more likely than dropping it soon.
